body:
## Summary

The owner's goal for disk-space-saviour is that everything safe to clear is clearable **by default**: caches, `node_modules` and similar files across the whole system, Playwright caches (but never their data directories), browser caches, Telegram's cache and other application caches.

A scan and a safe-tier clean of a macOS developer machine (`dss scan ~ /private/tmp`, 0.13.1) found these gaps. Each was measured on that machine.

## 1. Missing rules (caches not detected at all)

| Cache | macOS paths | Measured |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Telegram** (App Store / Mac app) | `~/Library/Group Containers/*.ru.keepcoder.Telegram/appstore/account-*/postbox/media/{cache,cache-storage,short-cache}`, `~/Library/Containers/ru.keepcoder.Telegram/Data/Library/Caches` | 192 MiB pure cache, 17 MiB container caches; the group container is 9.1 GiB in total |
| Telegram downloaded media | `…/postbox/media/*` outside the cache folders | 2.7 GiB. Re-downloadable from the cloud except secret-chat media, so a **moderate** tier with a clear description, not safe |
| Telegram Desktop | `~/Library/Application Support/Telegram Desktop/tdata/user_data/{cache,media_cache}` and the Linux/Windows equivalents | (not installed here) |
| **Chrome/Chromium on macOS, beyond the HTTP cache** | `~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/*/{Code Cache,GPUCache,DawnGraphiteCache,DawnWebGPUCache,Service Worker/CacheStorage,Service Worker/ScriptCache}`, `…/Chrome/{GrShaderCache,ShaderCache,component_crx_cache}` | 183 MiB (CacheStorage 164 MiB). Today's rule only has `~/Library/Caches/Google/Chrome/*/{Cache,Code Cache}`, and on macOS Code Cache lives under Application Support. The same applies to Brave, Edge, Arc, Opera, Vivaldi and Yandex. |
| **Safari / WebKit** | `~/Library/Caches/com.apple.Safari`, `~/Library/Containers/com.apple.Safari/Data/Library/Caches`, `~/Library/Caches/*/WebKit` | Protected by TCC: say clearly when Full Disk Access is missing rather than skipping silently |
| **Generic Electron / Chromium-embedded apps** | `~/Library/Application Support/<App>/{Cache,Code Cache,GPUCache,DawnGraphiteCache,DawnWebGPUCache,Service Worker/CacheStorage}` (and `~/.config/<App>/…`, `%APPDATA%\<App>\…`) | About 460 MiB across 14 apps here (Slack, Claude, Notion, Docker Desktop, opencode, LosslessCut, …). Only Discord, VS Code and its forks have rules. A generic rule, keyed on Electron markers such as a sibling `Local Storage`/`Preferences` and busy while the app runs, would cover all of them. |
| **AI-agent scratch space** | `/private/tmp/claude-<uid>/<project>/<session>/` of ended Claude Code sessions (git clones, sparse worktrees, logs), loose files left in `/tmp` by agent sessions, partial repository copies without `.git` in `/tmp` | 0.9 GiB in one session directory here, plus about 1.6 GiB of partial copies and probes in `/private/tmp`. `gh-issue-solver-workdirs` covers hive-mind; the same idea should cover Claude Code and Codex session scratch, with an inactivity window and the existing git safety checks. |

## 2. Defaults that are too conservative for "clearable by default"

- **`node_modules` of inactive projects is `moderate`, and of active projects `aggressive`.** It is ignored by git and re-created from the lockfile. For an inactive project with a lockfile and no running process, it could be in the default safe tier.
- **`node_modules` and `target` are blocked when the repository has uncommitted or unpushed work.** For example: "Git repository …/evirma-develop has 17 uncommitted changes" blocks `…/node_modules`; 69 items and 79 GiB were blocked here. Uncommitted source changes don't live in these ignored directories. Block only when the artifact directory itself holds untracked, non-ignored files, or when it is not ignored at all.
- **Playwright browsers:** only *old* revisions, and only in the moderate tier. Old revisions are re-downloaded on demand, so they could be in the safe tier.
  - The MCP profile directories (`~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/mcp-chrome-*`, user data) must never be touched.
  - Today they are excluded only because `versionPattern` happens not to match them. Add an explicit exclusion and a test that pins it.

## 3. Release

- npm `latest` is 0.13.1, but `main` is 0.14.0, so `npx disk-space-saviour@latest` does not run the newest fixes. Please publish, or make the release job fail loudly when the publish fails (compare #7).

## Expected

One `dss clean --tier safe --yes` (the default) clears all of the above that is re-creatable without user data loss. Data directories (Playwright MCP profiles, Telegram's message database, browser profiles) stay untouched, and each new rule has a test.
title: Clear every safe cache by default: Telegram, Chrome/Safari/Electron caches on macOS, agent scratch dirs, node_modules defaults, Playwright tiering
